follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $87.34 came from Premium and $12.66 from ads. Direct costs took $67.75 and running costs $21.00, other income added $0.52 and tax took $3.11, leaving $8.65 kept as profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Spotify reports in euros under IFRS. Dollar figures are converted at €1 = $1.0389 (ECB euro reference rate at Dec 31, 2024). As reported: revenue €4,242M · gross profit €1,368M · operating income €477M · net income €367M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago (+17% constant currency)

oneTimers: Operating expenses included €96M of 'social charges' — Swedish payroll taxes on share-based pay that swing with Spotify's share price — versus €33M a year ago, and the charges came in €80M above forecast as the share price rose, which is why operating income of €477M landed slightly below the €481M guidance.
Cost of revenue included €25M of real-estate impairment charges (€43M for the full year), which partly offset the Ad-Supported segment's gross-margin gains.

The 16% YoY drop in operating expenses flatters the comparison: a year ago the quarter carried efficiency charges from the late-2023 workforce restructuring, and lapping them contributed roughly 1,300 bps of the decline. Underneath that, personnel costs and marketing spend both fell.
The quarter carried a €132M income tax expense on €499M of pre-tax income — a 26.5% effective tax rate — versus a €61M tax benefit a year ago, when Spotify lost money.
otherDetail: Finance items netted +€22M — €127M of finance income against €105M of finance costs, a swing from a net €56M finance cost a year ago. The shareholder letter does not break the quarter's finance items down further.

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Subscriptions — 263 million people paying monthly, up 11% YoY; revenue per user (ARPU) €4.85, up 5% as price rises outweighed product mix; gross margin 34.7%.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising business — revenue grew 7% (6% in constant currency) on more ads sold, partly offset by softer pricing; its gross margin rose to 15.1% as music, podcast and other costs improved.

takeaways.text: Monthly active users grew 12% to 675 million — 35 million net additions, the largest Q4 in Spotify's history and 10 million above guidance. Premium subscribers rose 11% to 263 million, with 11 million net additions, 3 million above guidance. Ad-supported users grew 12% to 425 million.
takeaways.title: Record user growth

takeaways.text: Gross margin hit a record 32.2%, up 555 bps YoY. Premium gross margin reached 34.7% on audiobooks and music, and Ad-Supported gross margin rose to 15.1%. Operating income hit a record €477M, an 11.2% margin, versus a €75M loss a year ago — driving Spotify's first full year of operating profit (€1,365M).
takeaways.title: Margins hit record highs

takeaways.text: Free cash flow hit a record €877M, up 121% YoY, bringing full-year 2024 free cash flow to €2.3B and the cash pile to €7.5B. Net income swung to €367M from a €70M loss a year ago, helped by finance items swinging to a €22M net gain from a €56M net cost. Guidance for Q1 2025: 678M users, 265M subscribers, €4.2B revenue and €548M operating income.
takeaways.title: Cash piled up

verdict: Spotify grew revenue 16% to €4.24B (about $4.4B) and added a record 35 million monthly users, with operating income hitting a record €477M — capping its first full year of operating profit — and net income swinging to €367M from a €70M loss a year ago.
